reason: E2 directly demonstrates the exact hybrid-rolling process on the same alloy, achieving the claimed dual heterogeneous microstructure and reporting the specific strength-ductility combination. E1 provides supporting context on hierarchical constraint and microcrack-arresting mechanisms in lamellar EHEAs, but the key processing-structure-property link is fully established by E2.
premises: Cryo-rolling followed by warm-rolling at 600°C creates a dual heterogeneous microstructure in AlCoCrFeNi2.1
This dual heterogeneous microstructure yields an unprecedented combination of strength (~2000 MPa) and ductility (~8%)
The heterogeneous microstructure consists of retained lamellar and transformed nanocrystalline regions
The stored energy from cryo-rolling accelerates transformations during subsequent warm-rolling
Nanostructuring and refined interfaces increase back-stress and delay microcrack initiation
